subject: Temporary log-retention hold & subprocessor sync for imminent compliance audit
messages:
From: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@datacare.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: logs-ops@datacare.com
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary extension on ephemeral log purge for upcoming regulator inspection

Hi Hannah,

We have an unannounced regulator inspection next week in the EU for a small number of accounts. The audit team is asking us to preserve request-level debug logs for a 30-day window that would ordinarily be on a 7-day TTL. We understand Redwood's default ephemeral-log policy is 7 days for high-volume request traces; our security team is requesting a temporary hold on purge for the affected tenant IDs while the inspection runs (expected window: Aug 18 - Aug 27).

Two quick asks: 1) can Redwood apply a time-limited retention hold scoped to the tenant IDs I list in the attached PDF? 2) can you confirm whether any subprocessor (backup vendor / S3 mirror) will still sweep logs independently and whether we need a specific contract-side exception?

I've attached a brief request packet and a CSV of tenant IDs. Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Ellen Zhao
Head of Security Ops, DataCare Inc.
attachments: 20270814-dataproc-temp-hold-request.pdf, tenant_ids_dc_audit.csv

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@datacare.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-14T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension on ephemeral log purge for upcoming regulator inspection

Ellen — thanks for the heads up and the packet. We're sympathetic to audit needs and have a short form process for time-limited retention holds.

Immediate answers:
- We can place a scoped retention hold on the tenant IDs for up to 14 days via our internal purge-tagging system (we'll set a hard deadline to auto-release).
- However, some of our backup/subprocessor mirrors have an independent snapshot cadence; I need to confirm which subprocessors hold raw request logs beyond the 7-day TTL.

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll loop in Legal (Kimberly) to confirm whether we should record a DPA amendment or an exception memo.
2) Rishi (Infra) will check subprocessor inventory and snapshot sweep schedules, then respond with any required contract flags.

If that's agreeable, we'll confirm the exact window and provide an internal playbook for the hold (who can lift it, audit trail, and notification to your team).

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@datacare.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension on ephemeral log purge for upcoming regulator inspection

Team — thanks for the flag. A couple of legal notes up-front:
- A temporary operational hold is fine, provided we record the scope (tenant IDs), retention end-date, and an attested reason in our compliance ledger.
- If any subprocessor retains copies beyond our configured hold window, we need written confirmation from that vendor that they will honor the temporary scope. That vendor confirmation should be retained with the DPA amendment or an internal exception memo.

Action items for me: I'll draft a one-page exception memo (suitable for internal audit) describing the scope, timeline (we should prefer the shortest necessary window), and sign-off chain. Ellen, if you can confirm the exact tenant IDs and preferred expiry (DataCare suggested Aug 27), I'll get that memo out by end of day.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts — Redwood Inference
attachments: subprocessor_clause_template.docx

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@datacare.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-14T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension on ephemeral log purge for upcoming regulator inspection

Quick infra note and inventory summary:
- Primary serving logs: TTL=7 days (ephemeral). Purge is handled by internal job 'ephemeral-prune' daily at 02:00 UTC.
- Snapshot mirror to our cold-storage subprocessor (LogMirrorCo) runs nightly. Their copy retention is 90 days by default and they own the physical snapshots.
- We have a short-term option: tag the tenant IDs as "audit-retain-202708" which will prevent ephemeral-prune from deleting records; then issue a written hold to LogMirrorCo to freeze snapshot expiry for the scoped tenant IDs for 14 days.
- Caveat: LogMirrorCo's SLA requires 48hrs notice for snapshot-retention changes; they have an admin portal run by their ops team (ops@logmirrorco.net).

Proposed operational plan (if DataCare agrees):
1) Hannah to authorize a 14-day scoped hold with auto-expiry date set to Aug 28 23:59 UTC.
2) Rishi to open a ticket with LogMirrorCo and request a retention-freeze for tenant list; include a signed exception memo from Legal.
3) Marissa (CS) to confirm DataCare sees and acknowledges the hold and provide an internal contact for audit access.

I'll prepare the LogMirrorCo ticket as soon as Kimberly uploads the signed memo.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20270814.csv

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@datacare.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-14T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension on ephemeral log purge for upcoming regulator inspection

Ellen — confirming DataCare requests: keep request traces for tenant IDs in attached CSV on hold until Aug 28 23:59 UTC. Kimberly will produce the exception memo; Rishi will notify the subprocessor.

Please confirm you accept Aug 28 auto-release (we prefer a single auto-release to avoid indefinite holds). If you need an extension beyond Aug 28, we'll require formal follow-up with a justification and a Legal sign-off.

Action owners:
- Kim: exception memo + signature (today)
- Rishi: LogMirrorCo ticket + escalation (today)
- Marissa: customer acknowledgement and audit liaison (today)

Hannah

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Ellen Zhao <ellen.zhao@datacare.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-15T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension on ephemeral log purge for upcoming regulator inspection

Attached is the signed exception memo; I've also included a short DPA amendment snippet (language to append under Section 4.2: Data Retention & Subprocessors) confirming the temporary scoped hold and vendor acknowledgment requirement.

Text snippet (for internal record):
"Redwood Inference will apply a time-limited retention hold for the tenant identifiers specified by DataCare Inc. Retention hold shall automatically expire on 2027-08-28T23:59:00Z unless a written extension is provided and approved by Redwood Legal. Subprocessors who hold snapshots containing the scoped tenant data must confirm in writing that they will preserve such snapshots until the hold expiration; Redwood will retain these confirmations as part of the DPA exception record."

I've uploaded the memo and the signed CSV to the Drive folder (link below). Rishi, please include the Drive link in the LogMirrorCo ticket so they can reconcile tenant IDs against their snapshot index.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/compliance/DC-audit-2027-mpa

-Kim
attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20270814.csv, 20270814-dataproc-temp-hold-request.pdf
